![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Bug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bug-B71C1C) ![medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-medium-1A7BBE)


**Native Anthropic branch snapshots global fetch at build time**

`build()` runs during model construction, so the bare global `fetch` is snapshotted and any transport installed after — like the global.fetch patch in tests/e2e/lib/__tests__/integration-providers.test.ts:77-80 — no longer intercepts native Anthropic traffic. Read the ambient fetch lazily at call time by wrapping it in a function, or pass `fetch` only when `opts.fetch` is present.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/llm/providers/anthropic/index.ts, line 123:

Native Anthropic branch snapshots global fetch at build time

The native branch now always supplies a fetch by reading the bare global `fetch` at BUILD time (`withThinkingBindingRetry(opts?.fetch ?? fetch)`), whereas before it passed no `fetch` key when `opts.fetch` was absent and let the SDK resolve the ambient fetch per request. `build()` runs during model construction, so the global is snapshotted then: any consumer that installs its transport by replacing `global.fetch` after the model is built (the pattern used in tests/e2e/lib/__tests__/integration-providers.test.ts:77-80, which patches global.fetch to route requests to the mock provider server, and any redirect guard/proxy/interceptor wired the same way) no longer intercepts native Anthropic traffic — the stale pre-patch fetch is used and the request goes to the real endpoint. Resolve the ambient fetch lazily instead, e.g. `withThinkingBindingRetry(opts?.fetch ?? ((input, init) => fetch(input, init)))`, or only pass `fetch` when `opts.fetch` is present and apply the retry to the SDK's default path, so the ambient fetch is read at call time.
````

</details>

![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Bug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bug-B71C1C) ![high](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-high-6B6B92)


**Retry fabricates adaptive thinking when body has no thinking field**

Bodies with no `thinking` field get a fabricated `{ type: 'adaptive' }`, yet `anthropicModule.reasoning()` omits `thinking` for ids whose accepted shape is not adaptive (index.ts:256-269). The retried request then fails with a shape 400 instead of the binding 400, or silently re-enables thinking where effort is 'none'; merge `block_binding` only when `body.thinking` exists.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/llm/providers/anthropic/thinking-binding-retry.ts, lines 28-32:

Retry fabricates adaptive thinking when body has no thinking field

The retry builds `thinking` as `{ type: 'adaptive', ...body.thinking, block_binding }`, so when the outgoing body carried no `thinking` field at all it fabricates `{ type: 'adaptive', block_binding: ... }` instead of only adding the binding hint. `anthropicModule.reasoning()` omits `thinking` exactly for ids whose accepted shape is not adaptive (index.ts:256-269), so for those models the retried request goes out with the adaptive shape the module deliberately never sends — a shape 400 that replaces the binding 400 the retry was meant to fix — and on a thinking-by-default id it silently turns thinking back on for a slot whose effort is 'none'. Merge `block_binding` only when `body.thinking` is already present (and leave the field absent otherwise) rather than defaulting `type` to 'adaptive'.

Suggested code:

body.thinking = {
    ...body.thinking,
    block_binding: { prefix_mismatch_behavior: 'drop_block' },
};
````

</details>


<sub>Talk to Kody by mentioning @kody</sub>


<sub>Was this suggestion helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to help Kody learn from this interaction.</sub>

<!-- kody-codereview -->​
​

![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Performance](https://img.shields.io/badge/Performance-FF6D00) ![medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-medium-1A7BBE)


**Binding retry never remembers the refusal, wasting a 400 round trip per step**

The mismatch that triggers the refusal keeps matching, so every later request pays a wasted full-prompt round trip and a 400. Memoize in this wrapper's closure, per built model like libs/llm/rejected-reasoning-field.ts:11-16, that the model now needs `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior=drop_block` so the beta and option go up front.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/llm/providers/anthropic/thinking-binding-retry.ts, lines 20-23:

Binding retry never remembers the refusal, wasting a 400 round trip per step

The wrapper has no memory of the refusal, so the mismatch that caused it (the narrowed `activeTools` list plus the old signatures already in the message history) keeps matching and every later request in the same run is first uploaded in full, refused with a 400, and then re-sent — one wasted full-prompt round trip per step for the rest of the loop. Remember in this wrapper's closure (per built model, like the slot-level refusal memo in libs/llm/rejected-reasoning-field.ts:11-16) that this model now needs `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior=drop_block`, so the beta and the option are sent up front instead of paying a 400 per call.
````

</details>
